sources.entry: Ferron - Fast, memory-safe web server written in Rust. (Source Code) MIT Rust/Docker/deb

summary.one_liner: Ferron is a fast, memory-safe web server written in Rust, aimed at easy setup, automatic TLS, and request-level debugging in production.
summary.what_it_does: Ferron serves static files and acts as a reverse proxy, configured through a compact config file (ferron.conf). It issues and renews TLS certificates automatically. It records traces across layers of each request and links them to log entries, so trace IDs can be searched in log files. The CLI provides run, validate (check config without starting), adapt (output config as JSON), and daemon (Unix) commands. Packaging targets include archives, Debian and RPM packages, a Windows installer, and a Linux installer script, with a cross-build recipe available on Linux.
use_cases: debug requests with traces and logs
run a web server as a Unix daemon
notable: Automatic TLS certificate issuance and renewal
Traces link each request to related log entries; trace IDs searchable in logs
Compact, readable configuration syntax for sites and reverse proxies
Memory-safe by virtue of being written in Rust
Linux installer script and Debian, RPM, and Windows packaging recipes
caveats: Building from source requires cloning submodules and a Rust toolchain; cross-building is available on Linux only
Full directive reference lives in docs/configuration/ rather than the README
